- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (especially >0.80) — model tends to overshoot and fail to correct quickly.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative or neutral (especially <0.27 or 0.00) — model is overly optimistic in low-sentiment periods.
- Lag in price correction: model often delays downward adjustments after recent highs, especially when sentiment is high.
- Mean reversion bias: model overreacts to short-term volatility, underestimating long-term mean reversion in 30-day horizon.
- Overshoot after sharp upward moves: model frequently forecasts higher prices than true outcome after sentiment peaks, especially in 10–15 day windows.
- Sentiment-weighted adjustment: if sentiment >0.70, reduce forecast by 3–5% to avoid overconfidence; if sentiment <0.30, increase forecast by 2–4% to compensate for pessimism.
